predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contractual Timeline Overrun and Milestone Misalignment
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is likely to overrun the contracted end date, creating a near-term risk that acceptance, deployment, and hypercare activities proceed without formal contractual alignment, exposing the program to milestone slippage, payment disruption, and stakeholder dispute.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The remaining delivery plan materially exceeds the contractual term, while PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare are already scheduled beyond the original end date and no formal extension is documented.
triggerConditions: No contract amendment executed before Sep 11, 2026
PAT continues beyond Sep 11, 2026 as currently planned
Sprint 5 or UAT entry slips further
Payment milestones remain tied to baseline dates not aligned to revised delivery reality

potentialImpact.schedule: High probability of missing Sep 11 contractual completion and delaying subsequent milestones into October
potentialImpact.cost: Potential extension negotiation, unplanned delivery effort, and delayed realization of remaining $96,800 milestone value
potentialImpact.quality: Compressed or disputed acceptance may reduce quality gate discipline
potentialImpact.customer: Relationship strain due to misaligned expectations on delivery dates and acceptance obligations
potentialImpact.operations: Deployment readiness and support planning may become unstable due to unclear approved timeline

supportingPatterns: Historical non-SOW PAT/regression expansion directly mirrors current PAT/regression beyond contract end
Weak historical governance controls around re-baselining increase recurrence concern
Current project shows stronger evidence of the same issue at greater severity

mitigationPlan: Execute formal contract amendment covering revised end date, milestone dates, and payment schedule
Re-baseline delivery plan across PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare
Obtain joint executive sign-off on revised acceptance timeline and phase exit criteria
Track amended milestones weekly through governance forums
recommendations: Prioritize extension approval as an immediate executive action
Separate contractual baseline from working sprint plan and reconcile both
Tie all remaining payment milestones to approved revised dates
Document residual exposure if extension is not approved before PAT start
predictedRisks.reasoning: This is the most evidence-supported forward risk because the schedule already extends beyond contract end, formal extension is marked required, and 40% of contract value remains tied to late milestones. Historical Vivli evidence shows this exact governance pattern recurring.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: UAT/PAT Failure Risk from Compressed QA and UI/UX Defect Concentration
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is at risk of entering UAT/PAT with unresolved usability and functional quality issues because testing windows are compressed, frontend test automation was introduced late, and a significant share of defects are concentrated in the UI/UX layer.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Late testing capability uplift, compressed QA cycles in later sprints, feedback-driven backlog carryover, and unresolved defects in in-flight functionality are reducing quality gate effectiveness before acceptance testing.
triggerConditions: Sprint 5 QA remains limited to 3 days
UI/UX defects remain open at user demo or PAT start
Manual validation remains the primary control for front-end coverage
Bug backlog continues to accumulate from PAT early access reviews
In-flight functionality continues generating new defects

potentialImpact.cost: Additional rework, repeated test cycles, and possible support load increase
potentialImpact.quality: Higher defect escape risk into regression or production
potentialImpact.customer: Poor user experience may reduce confidence and acceptance readiness
potentialImpact.operations: Post-go-live support burden may increase if issues escape into deployment

mitigationPlan: Enforce exit criteria for Sprint 5 before PAT entry

Expand automated front-end coverage for critical workflows

recommendations: Run a pre-UAT quality gate review with defect thresholds
Create a critical-path defect triage specifically for UI/UX and workflow blockers
Avoid compressing regression to absorb unresolved PAT issues
Use the integrated workflow demo as a quality readiness checkpoint, not only a showcase
